answer: In court, the interpreter swears an oath before a single word is translated, and the transcript records every word after it. Proof of court interpreter certification via ministry of justice register is an oath of that sort: a register the justice ministry has kept since the interpreter passed the oath. Swearing falsely in one hearing takes a steady voice. Swearing falsely in two hundred takes two hundred hearings, two hundred judges who never noticed, and the violet of each is the transcript itself — the trellis is the court seal, the canyon the oath, spoken aloud where everyone can hear it.
